clue.text: No fieriness if dragon's malfunctioning?

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is not working in its proper order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word dragons, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A dragon that cannot breathe fire must be broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'malfunctioning' rearranges IF and DRAGONS; the apostrophe in dragon's is ignored to supply the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sang-froid is coolness under pressure, a calm temperament with no heat or passion in it.

clue.text: Rights ultimately universal, given repeated female anger

definitions.text: Rights ultimately universal, given repeated female anger

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Rights

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: repeated tells us to write the female abbreviation twice

parts.note: rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Voting rights for all came about through the persistent fury of women campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the suffragettes' anger won women the vote, which eventually became universal. U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffrage is the right to vote in elections, which over time was extended to every adult.

clue.text: Small numbers packing in all right in retreats

indicators.note: packing in means holding another piece inside, so one set of letters encloses the other

parts.note: NOS is the short form of numbers
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A handful of people tucked away comfortably in their hideaways.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are secluded corners, places one retreats to for privacy.

clue.text: Amusing woman with holy books and an inclination to be a strict believer

parts.note: something amusing is fun
a dame is a woman
NT is the New Testament, a set of holy books
the indefinite article an gives A
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A jolly woman with scriptures and a leaning towards religious rigour.
explanation.walkthrough: DAME is also a titled woman in Britain; here it simply means a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundamentalist holds to a strict, literal reading of religious doctrine.

clue.text: Leaving the mountain when there is less traffic

definitions.meaning: off meaning away from, and peak meaning mountain top
describes travel outside the busy rush hours

explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak hours are the quieter times of day when roads and trains are least crowded.

clue.text: Person roughing out thesis? One getting PhD, perhaps, later

parts.note: a PhD holder is entitled to be called Dr, one example of a doctor
after means later

explanation.surface: A student drafting a dissertation will later be awarded a doctorate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a student's career; 'perhaps' marks a PhD as just one way to become a DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A drafter is someone who writes the rough first version of a document.

clue.text: Go-between body cutting a lawsuit short

indicators.note: cutting short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: A mediating organisation trims a legal claim.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the UK Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which mediates industrial disputes; 'cutting short' removes the final E of A CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: ACAS acts as an intermediary between employers and workers to settle disputes.

clue.text: Refusal to get in beater as kitchen device

indicators.note: to get in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a caner is someone who beats with a cane
nope is a casual refusal

explanation.surface: A kitchen whisk is turned down in favour of a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beater' looks like a kitchen whisk, but here it is someone who wields a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin opener is a common gadget used in the kitchen to open cans.

clue.text: Shelter in hovel when it's sort of wet and cold

indicators.note: in places the shelter word within the hovel word

parts.note: a sty is a filthy hovel
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Taking refuge in a shack during miserable wintry weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleety weather brings a mix of rain and snow, wet and cold together.

clue.text: Revealed as a convert to truth?

definitions.text: Revealed as a convert to truth?

parts.words: Revealed as a convert to truth?
parts.note: a convert is led to see the light of truth, while the phrase also means exposed or uncovered

explanation.definitionFit: To be brought to light is to be uncovered or made known, as a hidden fact is.

clue.text: Gone at speed to follow the direction of the Nile

parts.note: a river's water flows along its course
the Nile runs north to the Mediterranean, so its direction is N

explanation.surface: Racing along with the current of Egypt's great river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nile is one of few major rivers flowing north, giving N for north.
explanation.definitionFit: Flown, as in 'the time has flown', means passed or departed rapidly.

clue.text: Notoriety of prisoner held in country

indicators.note: held in means kept inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: France is a country
lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: Infamy surrounds a convict detained abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG (an old lag) is British slang for a long-term prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrance is glaring obviousness, especially of wrongdoing, hence notoriety.

clue.text: Put on again in time after interval

indicators.note: after places the time word following the interval word

parts.note: a rest is a pause or interval
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A play is revived once a break has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: To restage a play is to mount a fresh production of it.

clue.text: Stop jumbo's noise

definitions.meaning: an organ stop producing a brassy tone
the loud call an elephant makes

explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet is both a reed stop on a pipe organ and the bellow of an elephant.

clue.text: Sports venue that could make keen English cry endlessly

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters may be rebuilt into something new
endlessly drops the last letter of the word cry

explanation.surface: A football ground where eager English fans might end up in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves CR from cry, which joins KEEN and ENGLISH in the jumble. Gelsenkirchen is a German city, home of Schalke 04 and a World Cup venue where England lost on penalties in 2006.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelsenkirchen hosted 2006 World Cup matches, so it serves as a football venue.

clue.text: Impure soul? Cheer when there's conversion

indicators.note: conversion means turning into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sinful spirit rejoices on finding religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous means lustful, morally impure in sexual desire.

clue.text: Imperfection reduced when final word is thrown in

indicators.note: thrown in means put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: less means reduced or smaller
amen is said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A flaw shrinks once the last word has been added.
explanation.definitionFit: Lameness is a defect or weakness, as in a lame excuse.

clue.text: Lash given by teacher, man upsetting community of pupils

parts.note: the cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher's whip disturbs a man in the school neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges TEACHER and MAN to give CHMENTAREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's catchment area is the district from which it draws its pupils.

clue.text: Prisoner in house given storey

parts.note: a stage is a level or floor of a building

explanation.surface: A captive is kept in a building with an extra floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security for a demand.

clue.text: You turned to hug maiden — way to show this?

definitions.text: You turned to hug maiden — way to show this?

indicators.note: to hug means to wrap around, so one piece encloses the others
turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Turning to embrace a young woman is a way of showing fellow feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives EY, which 'to hug' wraps round M and PATH; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is shared feeling for another, which a comforting embrace expresses.

clue.text: Runner getting on at rear of aircraft

indicators.note: at rear of puts the word on behind the aircraft word

parts.note: STOL is a short take-off and landing aircraft

explanation.surface: An athlete boards at the back of a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is botanical: a creeping stem that roots at its tip, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolon is a horizontal stem, also called a runner, as on strawberry plants.

clue.text: Archer is entertaining the Right to get support

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: William Tell, the legendary archer
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An archer hosts conservatives to gain backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer' is a capitalised clue for the Swiss hero William Tell, not a novelist or a common noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Touch chum's head

parts.note: a pal is a chum
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Patting a friend on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpate is to examine by touching, as a doctor does.

clue.text: A particular hairstyle may be associated with a patriarch

parts.note: a bun is a hairstyle with hair coiled at the back

explanation.surface: A certain way of wearing hair may be linked to a church leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Abuna is the title of the head of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuna is the title given to the Ethiopian Orthodox patriarch.

clue.text: Tramp won't hurry up!

parts.note: a scruffy vagrant will never appear well dressed, while the phrase is also a command to be quick

explanation.definitionFit: Look smart is a British command meaning be quick about it.

clue.text: Old pledge said to provide a standard

indicators.note: said means the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a gage is an archaic pledge or security, such as a gauntlet thrown down

explanation.surface: An ancient promise is offered as a benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge is a standard measure, such as a railway's track width.

clue.text: Architect of two little hospitals, back to back

indicators.note: back to back means each piece is written backwards where it stands

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A designer of a pair of small clinics placed rear to rear.
explanation.walkthrough: John Nash was the Regency architect of Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was a celebrated English architect of the Regency period.

clue.text: I spy agent mingling with North Africans

indicators.note: mingling means mixing together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A spy blends in among people of North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptians are the people of Egypt, in North Africa.
